Berkshire Hathaway nearly doubled its Lennar stake to about $2 billion, a bet on housing supply and a clean balance sheet despite slumping margins.

Berkshire trimmed Bank of America and Capital One while raising its Delta Air Lines stake 12%.

Stuart Miller said "our stock price is on sale," as Lennar repurchased 3 million shares at an average above today's price.

Released: The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income. It is a free guide from Fisher Investments covering what your retirement will really cost, where the cash flow should come from, and how much you can safely withdraw each year. Learn more here. Learn More Here › (sponsor)

Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK-B) raised its Class A share count in Lennar (NYSE:LEN) by 98.6% in the third quarter, according to the 13F it filed on Nov. 16. That took a stake worth about $1.2 billion at the prior quarter-end to roughly $2.1 billion as of Sept. 30.

Joe Raedle / Getty Images

Recent coverage reads the filing as an early look at the portfolio under Greg Abel, Warren Buffett's successor at Berkshire. The filing shows what changed by quarter-end. It doesn't show why the trades happened or exactly when.

Where Berkshire Pulled Back and Where It Leaned In

Berkshire also cut back on two lenders. It trimmed Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) and Capital One (NYSE:COF), according to Reuters. Even after the cut, Bank of America remained a top holding, with 455,860,908 shares worth $24.8 billion at quarter-end.

Berkshire added to Delta Air Lines (NYSE:DAL), raising its share count by 12% to 64,450,000 shares. Delta's premium revenue rose 18% last quarter even as fuel costs squeezed earnings. The new name in the filing is Bending Spoons, an Italian app company that went public in July. That position was worth $689 million at quarter-end, only about 0.2% of Berkshire's reported holdings.

title: Walmart's value proposition supports further market share gains, says Bank of America

Walmart's value proposition supports further market share gains, says Bank of America
Proactive
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 11:00 AM MST 2 min read
WMT
BAC

Walmart Inc (NYSE:WMT, XETRA:WMT) is positioned to gain further market share through its strengthening value, convenience and product assortment, according to Bank of America (BofA), which reiterated its 'buy' rating and raised its price objective to $141 from $139.

The bank said the retailer continued to gain share across product categories and income groups, led by higher-income households, while management described consumers as stable and resilient.

BofA expects the momentum to continue through the holiday season and beyond, despite an anticipated headwind from Health and Wellness pricing, which could reduce US comparable sales growth by approximately 125 to 150 basis points.

The analyst expects grocery inflation to accelerate from 1.4% in the latest quarter to the mid-2% range during 2027, assuming oil and commodity costs remain elevated.

Walmart's price rollbacks ended the third quarter at approximately 7,700, down from more than 11,000 in the second quarter but still above the historical range of 5,000 to 5,500, helping the retailer achieve some of its strongest food market share gains in three years.

Learn more about Walmart

Read more about Walmart

Walmart+ membership also expanded at a double-digit rate in the first few weeks after the Sam's Club Plus bundle launch, while bundled members increased their online Walmart spending by more than 80% compared with pre-launch levels.

The bank highlighted advertising and marketplace operations as additional growth engines, with US advertising revenue rising 37% and marketplace sales increasing 49%.

VIZIO's expanding installed base and integration of Vibe offer further advertising opportunities, while its television operating system powered the best-selling TV models in the US, with unit volumes rising nearly 150% year on year.

For fiscal 2028, the bank forecasts net sales growth of 4.8% and operating income growth of 8.3%, raising its earnings estimates to $3.20 per share.

The fair value estimate for Expeditors International of Washington has shifted from US$187.93 to US$195.40, indicating that a higher price target is now being used in current models. Analysts attribute this to Q3 2026 revenue and earnings that were ahead of prior expectations, as well as stronger air and ocean freight trends that have influenced recent research updates. What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Several firms have raised fair value assumptions after Expeditors International of Washington hosted its first investor day in over a decade. UBS, BofA and Citizens cited strong Q3 results, supportive freight markets and margin productivity opportunities.

UBS and BofA highlight the company's multi year earnings ambitions and AI driven productivity plans. They view Expeditors International of Washington as structurally well positioned in air and ocean freight, with updated targets incorporated into their higher valuation work.

Citizens points to market share efforts and new growth verticals, while TD Cowen and Stifel reference capital allocation and technology upgrades as key supports for the refreshed long term framework presented to investors.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Morgan Stanley, Barclays, Goldman Sachs and BNP Paribas maintain more cautious stances. They question visibility on the new long term objectives, freight rate sustainability and whether current earnings power for Expeditors International of Washington is close to a cyclical peak.

Key Takeaways

Of the 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 10 bought Bank of America and 16 sold. Dan Loeb's Third Point was one of the buyers.

The Wellcome Trust and Mirova were the two biggest buyers, and both ended the quarter with even more money in JPMorgan Chase.

The 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the quarter so far are those with $1 billion or more of US stocks or a name readers know, leaving out quant and index funds. Of those, 10 bought Bank of America, either opening a position or adding 20% or more. Sixteen sold out or cut 20% or more, and 61 held it at the quarter's end.

The buyers started from scratch

All three of the biggest buyers opened new positions. The Wellcome Trust, whose 13F holds $9.16 billion of US stocks, bought 2.55 million shares worth $139 million at Sept. 30. The Wellcome Trust and Mirova also bought JPMorgan Chase (JPM:NYSE), and both ended the quarter with more money in it than in Bank of America: $149 million at the Wellcome Trust, and $227 million at Mirova, which raised its JPMorgan share count 2,066%.

title: Can Bank of America Sustain Its Robust Capital Returns in 2027?
detail:
Can Bank of America Sustain Its Robust Capital Returns in 2027?
Nikita Kataruka
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:32 AM MST 3 min read
BAC
WFC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America BAC continues to emphasize shareholder returns through consistent dividend increases and substantial share repurchases. Following the 2026 Federal Reserve stress test, the bank raised the quarterly dividend 14.3% to 32 cents per share, marking its sixth consecutive annual hike. In third-quarter 2026, BAC returned $8.3 billion to its shareholders, comprising $6 billion in common share repurchases and $2.2 billion in dividends.

The bank's solid earnings and capital position provide a foundation for sustaining these distributions. Its common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio stood at 10.9% as of Sept. 30, 2026, down from 11.2% in the preceding quarter but above regulatory requirements. Moreover, net income increased 7.6% year over year to $24.6 billion during the first nine months of 2026, strengthening its capacity to fund shareholder returns.

BAC's robust liquidity and funding profile further support its capital return prospects. As of Sept. 30, 2026, the bank held $250 billion in cash and cash equivalents, while average global liquidity sources totaled $914 billion in the third quarter. Its deposit base exceeding $2 trillion provides stable funding and financial flexibility to support business expansion alongside shareholder distributions.

The bank's latest quarterly dividend declaration of 32 cents per share, payable on Dec. 24, 2026, reinforces its commitment to capital returns. Continued repurchases could also support earnings per share. However, regulatory capital requirements, including the G-SIB surcharge, and the need to maintain adequate capital buffers could influence future distributions.

Looking ahead to 2027, BAC appears well-positioned to sustain meaningful shareholder returns, supported by recurring earnings, substantial liquidity and diversified revenue streams. Nevertheless, elevated operating expenses, potential credit deterioration and regulatory uncertainties could constrain buybacks. Balancing capital distributions with growth investments and financial stability will remain crucial.

How Do JPM and WFC Compare With BAC?

JPMorgan Chase JPM distributed $4.4 billion in common dividends and recorded $664 million in net common share repurchases during third-quarter 2026. In September, JPMorgan raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $1.65 per share, while its standardized CET1 ratio stood near 14%. Despite JPM's $50 billion repurchase authorization, management has moderated buybacks to prioritize franchise investments.

Wells Fargo WFC repurchased approximately $2.5 billion in common shares during third-quarter 2026, bringing its nine-month repurchases to $9.6 billion. WFC also increased its quarterly dividend to 50 cents per share and retained approximately $20.2 billion in repurchase authorization as of Sept. 30, 2026. Wells Fargo's capital strength supports continued shareholder distributions, subject to regulatory requirements and investment needs.

Strategists led by Michael Hartnett said risk assets are struggling as excess bullishness collides with 71 global rate hikes between June 2026 and May 2027. A credit and stock slump, with investment-grade CDX above 80 basis points and the S&P 500 below 6,845, could cut the cycle short if the Fed still treats stocks as "too big to fail," they said.

But voters used the midterms to demand affordability. If the Fed now acts as an inflation hawk, the March 18 and April 28 meetings are the earliest investors can price in the end of hikes, and hard landing risks grow, the strategists said.

Markets are now trading "post-bubble," a pattern like 2000, when tech peaked and the Fed kept hiking into a 2001 recession, they noted. Hard landing odds are too low and consensus 2027 forecasts for 5% to 6% nominal GDP growth and over 15% earnings growth are too high. Jobless claims above 250,000 and investment-grade spreads above 100 basis points would signal a "doom loop," they said.
